canonicalReview.reconciliationSummary: The two reviewers disagree only on F-EPIC-001 (epic-reviewer-2's blocker); everything else is complementary. Independent re-verification sustains the blocker: against a clean default registry, `node dist/cli.js threads new-thread --file-path ''` returned `{ ok: true, value: { threadId: "th_bd276835dfc0a9a2", filePath: "" } }`, `threads resolve` returned that row, and `intake-stream list-events --thread-id th_bd276835dfc0a9a2` failed with `{ errorClass: "caller_error", code: "thread_not_found", reason: "no thread file exists at " }` — a registry row with no durable thread file, on the real SDK and built CLI. Three pieces of evidence harden it beyond reviewer-2's report: (1) the code's own comment at src/domains/threads/index.ts:66-69 calls the no-row-without-file invariant 'absolute', and the Story 1 boundary note in epic.md makes the same demand; (2) the CLI guard comment at src/cli/index.ts:99-100 explicitly names the empty-path/temp-database hazard, but the guard checks only `flags.filePath === undefined`, so an empty string slips past — the failure mode was known and the defense is incomplete; (3) the intake envelope's ThreadRefSchema (validate.ts:38) requires NonEmptyString for filePath while newThread accepts any string, an internal inconsistency on the same contract. No test covers an empty path (test/threads.test.ts has none). epic-reviewer-1's pass is explained by not probing this edge, not by contrary evidence, so per the conservative rule the blocker is not downgraded. All of epic-reviewer-1's non-blocking findings were independently re-verified in the current code and retained; reviewer-2's F-EPIC-002 and reviewer-1's NB-3 describe the same read-back ref-validation gap at the CLI and SDK layers respectively and are merged into one finding. Both reviewers' gate claims were re-run and confirmed: verify-all exits 0 (build, typecheck, lint OK over 42 files, boundaries OK over 38 files, 16 files / 111 tests passing).
crossStoryFindings: The five stories compose into the designed pipeline: pure pre-lock validation → BEGIN IMMEDIATE → corruption check → per-event dedup/record/turn-transition/projection-with-membership-stamp/work-queueing → result assembly → COMMIT (src/domains/intake-stream/internal/pipeline.ts), with deterministic ids (m<eventOrder>, t<turnOrder>, w-<sourceId>-<kind>) consistent across stories and naturally idempotent for Epic 02.

Story 1's thread-creation contract has a confirmed hole that every later story inherits: an empty file path registers a thread with no durable file, after which all thread-scoped operations on that id fail with thread_not_found. Later stories' substrate-building through Story 1's real surface is exactly why this single-surface defect is epic-wide (F-EPIC-001).

Rigor drift across read surfaces: messageEvents and listEvents validate the thread reference against the closed ThreadRef schema, but listMessages, listTurns, and both listQueuedWork operations skip validateThreadRef, and the corresponding CLI commands skip the required-flag guard the intake commands have — fail-closed behavior is preserved but the error vocabulary differs (merged finding F-EPIC-002).

Later stories' tests build state through earlier stories' real surfaces (thread creation via newThread, events via messageEvents), giving continuous upstream re-verification; no story mocks a neighbor.
architectureFindings: Module structure matches the tech-design layout (domains/{threads,intake-stream,messages,turns} with index.ts + internal/, tech-utils, shared, cli, sdk.ts); the boundary gate passes: 'boundaries: OK (38 files checked, fixtures exempt)', with test/fixtures/ as the sanctioned below-SDK exemption.

Thread creation validates nothing about the path beyond existsSync (src/domains/threads/index.ts:73); node:sqlite's DatabaseSync('') opens a temporary database, so createThreadFile succeeds without producing a durable file, and the registry row lands anyway — violating the invariant the same file's comment calls absolute. The intake envelope already types filePath as NonEmptyString (validate.ts:38), so the fix aligns newThread with an existing contract decision rather than inventing one.

Sound beyond-design addition: thread-file schema is a versioned migration history (v1 events → v4 work items) with lazy upgrade and identity validation before migration (threads/internal/create.ts), consistent with file-is-authority and well-tested.

Benign interface drift: messages.createFromEvent takes a third turnId parameter versus the design's two-arg signature — the natural realization of the design's stamp-after-transition rule; turns.applyEvent matches the design exactly.

Epic-vs-design contract drift: epic Flow 4 declares empty required payload fields invalid, but validate.ts types text and tool_result.content as Schema.String (validate.ts:55, 63) per the tech design's plain-string interfaces, so empty strings pass while empty actor/harness/idempotencyKey/toolCallId/toolName are rejected via NonEmptyString (NB-1, needs human ruling).

Transaction boundaries, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, file-then-row creation with compensation, registry lazy-init with non-creating reads, tokenizer pinning (js-tiktoken o200k_base recorded in thread metadata), and the operation-context shape match tech-design decisions 2, 3, 6, and 8.
epicCoverageAssessment: All 33 TCs from the epic appear as greppably-tagged passing tests across Flows 1–5, including both named cross-chunk deferrals closed in their owing stories (TC-1.4 in intake.test.ts; the TC-3.3/TC-3.6 work halves in work-queue.test.ts) and all eight architecture-risk rows from the test plan.

Confirmed coverage gap behind the blocker: no test exercises an empty file path on threads.newThread or `threads new-thread --file-path ''`, so AC-1.1/AC-1.3/AC-1.4 are proven only for non-degenerate paths; test/threads.test.ts has no such case.

Test quality is substantive: durability asserted through raw SQL row scans, rejection asserted through full five-surface logical read-back diffs against baselines, the 300KB tool-result round-trip runs through both SDK and spawned-binary stdin.
111 tests across 16 files versus the plan's ~72 estimate; the overage is migration tests, per-story CLI-process splits, and supplemental strictness cases, all in-scope.

Both gates re-verified by this canonical pass: verify-all (epic gate) exits 0 end to end including the spawned-binary CLI suite; green-verify's Red-manifest immutability check was reported passing by both reviewers.
productionPathFindings: No fake adapters, mocks, or stubbed success on the production path: storage is real node:sqlite (WAL, foreign keys, busy_timeout), token counting is real js-tiktoken o200k_base, and every CLI command body is one SDK call plus JSON rendering.

Material production-path defect (the blocker): the real SDK and built CLI create a registry row for an empty path with no thread file; reproduced this pass as `{ ok: true, value: { threadId: "th_bd276835dfc0a9a2", filePath: "" } }` followed by thread_not_found on read-back. The CLI's own guard comment names this exact hazard but only catches a missing flag, not an empty value (src/cli/index.ts:99-103).

Two module-level test seams live in the production pipeline module (setIntakeWalkHook, setIntakeClock — pipeline.ts:23, 34): null/no-op in production, settable only through the boundary-exempt fixtures directory, fail-safe when unset; the walk hook is sanctioned by the test plan's architecture-risk row, the clock setter is an addition. Neither fakes success (NB-4).

Dead code and stale artifacts: shared/errors.ts:36 notImplemented() has no remaining callers; dist/ retains pre-epic compiled output (dist/commands/, dist/thread-events/, dist/token-counting/) not produced by current src/ — the package is private so nothing ships, but tsc does not clean (NB-5).

newThread stamps createdAt from the raw wall clock with no injection seam (threads/index.ts:85), a small departure from the test plan's claim that the injected clock covers createdAt; production behavior is correct.

blockingFindings.title: Thread creation accepts an empty path and registers a thread with no durable file
blockingFindings.evidence: src/domains/threads/index.ts:73 guards only with existsSync(input.filePath); node:sqlite's DatabaseSync('') opens a temporary database that vanishes on close, so newThread({ filePath: '' }) succeeds and inserts a registry row for filePath ''. Independently reproduced on the built CLI against a clean default registry: `threads new-thread --file-path ''` → { ok: true, value: { threadId: 'th_bd276835dfc0a9a2', filePath: '' } }; `threads resolve` returned the row; `intake-stream list-events --thread-id th_bd276835dfc0a9a2` → { errorClass: 'caller_error', code: 'thread_not_found', reason: 'no thread file exists at ' }. This violates the no-row-without-file invariant the code itself documents as 'absolute' (threads/index.ts:66-69) and the Story 1 boundary note in epic.md, and breaks AC-1.1 (no file created), AC-1.3 (no file to read the id from), and AC-1.4 (row points at nothing). Corroborating evidence the hazard was known: the CLI guard comment at src/cli/index.ts:99-100 names the empty-path/temp-database failure mode, but the guard checks only `flags.filePath === undefined`, so an empty string passes; and the intake envelope's ThreadRefSchema already requires NonEmptyString for filePath (validate.ts:38) while newThread accepts any string. No test covers the empty-path case on SDK or CLI. Fix is small and contract-aligned: reject empty (or whitespace-only) filePath in newThread with a caller_error before any storage touch, plus SDK and CLI tests.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Empty-string payload text/content accepted despite epic Flow 4's 'missing or empty required field' rule
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Epic Flow 4 lists 'a missing or empty required field: idempotency key, actor, harness, or the payload fields its kind requires' as invalid. validate.ts types text and tool_result.content as Schema.String (validate.ts:55, 63), so { text: '' } and empty tool_result content pass validation, while empty toolCallId/toolName/actor/harness/idempotencyKey are rejected via NonEmptyString. The tech design's interfaces typed these as plain string, so the drift originates between epic and design; the implementation followed the design. Whether an empty tool result (a real occurrence) should be a rejection is a product call.

nonBlockingFindings.title: CLI parses flags with strict:false, silently ignoring unknown or misspelled flags
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: src/cli/index.ts:53-64 calls parseArgs with strict: false, so `lhc threads new-thread --file-path p --titel x` creates the thread with no title and no error. This is the silent-drop failure mode the epic's boundary philosophy ('Nothing is silently dropped') exists to prevent, though the closed-contract rule formally covers the event envelope, not argv. A strict: true parse with a structured usage error would align the CLI boundary with the SDK boundary's strictness.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Read-back surfaces skip thread-reference validation at both SDK and CLI layers
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Merged from epic-reviewer-1 NB-3 and epic-reviewer-2 F-EPIC-002 — the same gap at two layers. SDK: messageEvents and listEvents validate the thread reference against the closed ThreadRef schema (pipeline.ts:92, 267), but listMessages, listTurns, and both listQueuedWork operations pass the reference straight to resolveThreadRef, so unknown fields or an empty filePath are tolerated. CLI: `messages list`, `messages list-queued-work`, `turns list`, and `turns list-queued-work` (cli/index.ts:176-183) lack the --thread-id/--file-path missing-flag guard the intake commands have, and threadRefFrom defaults a missing path to '' (cli/index.ts:79); verified this pass that `node dist/cli.js messages list` returns thread_not_found for an empty path instead of a usage error. Behavior remains fail-closed; the inconsistency is in which error the caller gets and whether unknown ref fields are named.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Mutable test seams exported from the production pipeline module
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: setIntakeWalkHook and setIntakeClock (pipeline.ts:23, 34) are module-global mutable state in production code, reachable by any importer of the internal module path even though the boundary check confines them to test/fixtures and the package export map exposes only the SDK root. Unset they are inert (real wall clock when unset; explicit clock argument wins). The walk hook is design-sanctioned by the test plan's architecture-risk row; the clock setter is an addition beyond the design's context-injected clock. Consider relocating behind a single test-only entry or documenting them in the design's seam inventory when Epic 02 extends the context.
